correctness.rationale: The bracket identity \([x,y]=x_1(y_1+y_2)z\) gives the four necessary-and-sufficient equations \(a(a+c)=a(b+d)=t\), \(b(a+c)=b(b+d)=0\). Over any field a vanishing outer product forces one factor to vanish, and a nonzero outer product forces the two row eigenvectors. This proves the three affine components and their intersections over arbitrary characteristic. The rank strata follow from the row space of a rank-one \(2\times2\) block; idempotents from rank-one projections; nilpotents from trace zero in two rank-one branches. The checker exhaustively confirms direct homomorphism equivalence for all \(3\times3\) matrices over \(\mathbf F_2\) and \(\mathbf F_3\), and separately enumerates the whole parametrized union over \(\mathbf F_5\). The verified results include counts, ranks, idempotents and nilpotents. The characteristic-two boundary is explicitly included. The proof concerns only the reduced variety and makes no claim about the unreduced scheme.

value.rationale: This is the complete endomorphism monoid geometry of the canonical three-dimensional nilpotent Leibniz example whose automorphism group was already studied. The unexpected feature is that the closure of all invertible endomorphisms misses two entire top-dimensional components. The exact arbitrary-field component decomposition simultaneously determines rank strata, retracts, idempotents, nilpotents, and a uniform finite-field zeta function. These are natural structural invariants of an endomorphism monoid rather than an arbitrary small numerical slice.
